chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, who said:

We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and the House (the Kaaba) was crammed with its people. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not from us, the one who does not have good companionship with the one who accompanies him, and friendly association with the one who associates with him, and eating together with the one who eats with him, and sharing living space with the one who shares living space with him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four key aspects of good companionship mentioned by Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: In a crowded gathering, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links spiritual identity to social grace, using four distinct terms—suhbah, murafiqah, mumalaha, and mukhalata—to describe the spectrum of communal life from general companionship to shared domestic life. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on 'adab al-mujtama' (social etiquette), teaching that true adherence to the Imam extends beyond ritual to include kindness and patience in daily interactions with neighbors and peers. It reflects the broader Shia ethical framework where social cohesion is a manifestation of religious devotion.
